correctness.rationale: For finite nonempty unvalued equivalence frames P,Q, forth forces each source equivalence block C to map inside a target block D, while back makes f:C onto D. Globally onto iff every target block is hit by at least one source block. Source relabelings reduce individual onto maps from a size-a block to positive fiber compositions (j,u_1,...,u_(b_j)) and collections to multisets of length r_a. Target automorphisms H permute equal-size blocks and target points, so two-sided diagram classes are H-orbits of these multisets with coverage. An h-fixed multiset must be constant on each cyclic h-orbit of profiles; each orbit length d contributes (1-z^d)^(-1). Inclusion–exclusion on h-cycles of destination blocks enforces coverage, and Burnside averaging proves the coefficient formula. For fixed target and fixed finite source-size support, finite rational generating functions give eventual multivariate quasipolynomials with coordinate periods dividing exponent H. Exactly kernel elements of H acting trivially on all available profiles contribute top total degree; losing a reachable block or nontrivial h action lowers degree, yielding |K|/|H| prod r_a^(q_a-1)/(q_a-1)!. When Q fixed, profile enumeration and DP coefficient extraction are polynomial in source size; target size must stay fixed. Independently reproduced the elementary source-two-blocks-size3 to target one-block-size2 example: exactly two symmetry-reduced orbits, and inspected all three Python implementations and finite comparison logs (278 direct-frame pairs, 55 full-group cases, 45 special-family cases). The finite data do not prove the universal formula.
